guards.guard: the p50 is a stable statistic over the window
guards.observed: It is not, and this is the guard that changed the item's conclusion. Quarter-hour p50 rises 1,182 -> 2,701 -> 3,536 -> 5,538 and then PLATEAUS at 5,449 / 5,351. A whole-session p50 is an average over a rising-then-flat curve and lands wherever you stopped measuring: it read 3,334 ms at n=60 and 4,328 ms at n=89, from the same session. Neither is the steady-state cost; ~5,400 ms is.

guards.guard: the reported number is stable against how long I measured

guards.guard: tape volume comparable to the baseline session

Today's Last1 rows span 503 to 26,107 within one hour, and prepare_ms tracks that growth closely. Without the baseline's row count the two are not comparable, and the -46.2% cannot be attributed.

notes:
READ THE PLATEAU NUMBER, NOT THE SESSION p50: steady-state prepare_ms settles at ~5,400 ms against a 6,199 ms baseline, i.e. about -13%. The session p50 (-30.2%) and the 60-roll p50 (-46.2%) are both artefacts of averaging across a tape that was still filling.

WHY THIS ITEM WAS FILED TWICE. I first filed it at n=60 with p50 3,334 ms and a -46.2% delta. Continuing to sample to n=89 moved the p50 to 4,328 ms and the delta to -30.2%, and -- more usefully -- showed the quarter-hour curve FLATTENING at 5,449 / 5,351 after rising to 5,538. So the drift is bounded, not runaway, and the settled value is the one worth quoting. Both passes are kept above because the gap between them is the finding: a 46% improvement and a 13% improvement came from the same session, the same flag and the same pod, and differed only in when I stopped counting.

ORIGINAL n=60 ANALYSIS, retained:

THE HEADLINE NUMBER IS -46.2% (p50 3,334 ms vs 6,199 ms baseline) AND I DO NOT BELIEVE IT MEANS WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE.

Three reasons, all measured:

1. THE p50 IS NOT STATIONARY. It climbs monotonically through the session: 1,182 / 2,701 / 3,536 / 5,538 ms by quarter-hour. The final quarter-hour's p50 (5,538 ms) is within 11% of the 6,199 ms baseline. So 'we are 46% faster' and 'we are level with baseline' are both supportable from today's data depending on which 15 minutes you quote — which means the session p50 is the wrong summary statistic for this quantity.

2. prepare_ms TRACKS TAPE VOLUME, and tape volume grew 52x during the window. Last1 raw_rows went 503 -> 26,107 between 09:30 and 10:19. The drift in (1) is not mysterious; it is the tape filling up. A p50 measured over a window that starts at the open is therefore weighted toward the cheapest builds of the day.

3. THE BASELINE DOES NOT RECORD ITS OWN TAPE VOLUME. The bundle gives n=25 and the flag state, not the hour or the row count. Comparing 3,334 ms against 6,199 ms is comparing two numbers whose main driver is unrecorded on one side. If the baseline was taken late in a session, the true improvement is smaller than -46%; if early, larger.

ON THE COMPONENT SAVING: the observed -2,865 ms session delta is about 2.1x the ~1.34 s component saving the bundle quotes, so it is NOT simply explained by that component. Given (1)-(3) I would not treat the excess as a real additional win — the more parsimonious reading is that the two measurements sit at different points on the same rising curve.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: compare like-for-like on raw_rows rather than on clock time. Today's data supports that directly — e.g. the 10:12:39 build at 22,198 rows took 5,186 ms. A baseline row count is the one missing input.
